intro.title: Write Promise all from scratch
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build your own version of the Promise.all method from scratch using plain JavaScript. You'll learn how to handle multiple promises simultaneously and return a single promise that resolves only when all input promises are successful. The core concept involves working with asynchronous operations, promise states, and array manipulation. You'll use key JavaScript constructs like the Promise constructor, then, catch, and array methods such as map and reduce. By the end, you'll understand how Promise.all works internally and how to implement robust error handling for promise-based workflows.
intro.usecase: Promise.all is essential when you need to fetch multiple data sources simultaneously before rendering a complete UI. For example, a dashboard might need to load user profile data, recent notifications, and analytics metrics concurrently before displaying the full interface. In e-commerce checkout flows, Promise.all can validate payment details, check inventory, and calculate shipping costs in parallel before confirming the order. This pattern prevents partial loading states and ensures all required data is available before proceeding with user interactions.

objectives: Construct a custom Promise.all function that accepts an array of promises
Initialize a results array to store resolved values in order
Implement promise resolution tracking using a counter
Integrate error handling to reject immediately when any promise fails
Manipulate the results array to maintain input order of resolved values
Control the flow of asynchronous operations to wait for all promises
Apply the custom Promise.all to handle multiple asynchronous tasks

steps.hint: Focus on understanding the core behavior: Promise.all waits for all promises to succeed or fails fast if any promise fails.
